source.title: Neural Theory-of-Mind? On the Limits of Social Intelligence in Large LMs
source.authors: Maarten Sap; Ronan Le Bras; Daniel Fried; Yejin Choi

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including the March 2023 added appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream benchmark accuracy across model sizes and training setups, rather than held-out cross-entropy scaling laws or compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The study measures Social IQa and ToMi question-answering accuracy and compares results across GPT-3 sizes and later OpenAI models. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, test extrapolation of loss, or measure compute-optimal parameter/token splits. Cited scaling-law results and cited BIG-Bench/PaLM results are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The main experiments compare three GPT-3 sizes (ada, curie, davinci) on two downstream benchmarks, Social IQa and ToMi. That is a scale-versus-downstream-accuracy result in a new task setting, so it bears on V6. It does not measure loss, fit curves, or report parameter counts. The 2023 appendix compares post-training regimes (IFT, RLHF, chat) and GPT-4, not scale, so it does not bear on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The paraphrase should add that the authors explicitly find only small gains from scaling GPT-3 (ada to davinci) on both tasks. They use this to argue that scale alone is unlikely to yield Theory of Mind.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benchmark question-answering accuracy and model comparisons rather than held-out language-model loss sweeps, power-law fits, or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Social IQa accuracy varies with model size, number of few-shot examples, probing type (LM versus MC), and whether questions concern the main or other participants. ToMi results vary by question type (factual versus mental-state), belief type, order, and number of examples; the newer-model comparison uses a randomly selected 400-example subset and zero-shot prompting.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction-tuning and RLHF raise Social IQa zero-shot accuracy (45% to 53–55% with LM scoring; 60–79% with multiple-choice probing). ToMi mental-state accuracy stays near 60%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training regime (IFT/RLHF), not pretraining scale, changes downstream social-reasoning accuracy.

record.code_released: http://maartensap.com/neuralToM (preprocessed datasets; code release not stated)
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2022)
record.problems: The evidence concerns two English benchmarks rather than loss scaling or broad downstream generalization. The authors note that ToMi is automatically constructed, the original models were accessed through an API, and newer-model training details are opaque. The newer comparison uses 400 randomly selected examples; possible benchmark-data contamination, including a GPT-4 data-contamination disclosure, prevents firm conclusions. Several detailed results appear only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Did not transcribe individual plotted points for every k value or all figure-only breakdowns by Social IQa reasoning dimension and ToMi question subtype (Figures 2–6, 8–12); retained the textual comparisons and numerical results stated in the paper. BIG-G and PaLM results in Appendix A are reported as prior-work results and were not entered as study results.

untested.parts: Predictability itself: no fitted accuracy-versus-scale curve, no stated parameter counts, no relation to pretraining loss; only three sizes on two benchmarks.
All of it: no pretraining loss.

missing.what: GPT-3 size comparison on ToMi FACT questions: ada struggles while curie and davinci are near-perfect.

record.verdict_notes: Parameter counts are never stated. The BIG-G and PaLM numbers are cited from BIG-Bench and were correctly excluded. The appendix models differ in training regime rather than known scale, so they were unlinked from V6.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute sweep.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute comparison or parameter/token allocation sweep.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No test of power-law scaling in other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning loss, or transfer loss.

Tests accuracy on two English ToM/social-reasoning benchmarks, not a broad range of downstream tasks or a relationship to measured pretraining loss. Does not fit a predictive accuracy-versus-scale curve.
No comparison of fitted scaling exponents or optimal splits under alternative counting, schedule, data, or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: GPT-3 ada/curie/davinci on Social IQa and ToMi mental-state questions, few-shot LM scoring
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with size, but the authors call the gains small or very small and far from human level: about 55% on Social IQa; ToMi MIND peaks at 60% versus at most 55% for smaller models (r1, r2, r3, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy improves only modestly, reaching about 55% on Social IQa and 60% on ToMi mental-state questions versus at most 55% for smaller models.

relationships.condition: GPT-3 sizes on ToMi factual questions (text, Appendix B.2 / Fig 8; no row)
relationships.reason: Curie and davinci reach near-perfect FACT accuracy while ada struggles, a clear size effect. Based on the text; no row records it.
relationships.display_finding: Curie and davinci reached near-perfect factual accuracy, while ada struggled.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-3 size comparison on Social IQa and ToMi, as described in the main results
reader_labels.reason: The largest tested GPT-3 model performs better than the smaller GPT-3 models on these benchmark tasks, though the reported gains are small (r1–r7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ToMi mental-state questions and newer instruction-tuned/chat models
reader_labels.reason: Mental-state accuracy remains around 55–60%; GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 score 60% and 59%, respectively, and the reported overall ToMi gains for IFT/RLHF are attributed to factual questions (r6, r7, r15–r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy is higher for the newer systems, but the study identifies possible training-data contamination and reports a character-focus difference, so these outcomes do not establish general downstream predictability (r12–r14).
